answer: A head is admitted only if its spiral carries signatures from karsts that never communicate, and each karst signs a given root once. The spiral's length sets the quorum: the k-th head of one root needs k+1 fresh karsts the operator cannot command. Every signature costs velvet, which the signing karst keeps if that head is judged a clone. One head needs one karst and one velvet; a holder of a thousand heads spends 500,500 velvet across them.
